symbols.name: \(\epsilon\)
symbols.def: Fixed lower bound on both treatment probabilities.

symbols.name: \(\rho_\epsilon\)
symbols.def: Positive constant depending only on \(\epsilon\) that bounds the proved range \(d\le \rho_\epsilon n\log(en)\).

symbols.name: \(c_\epsilon\)
symbols.def: Positive lower-bound constant depending only on \(\epsilon\) whose existence is asserted by the risk statements.

symbols.name: \(C_\epsilon\)
symbols.def: Finite upper-bound constant depending only on \(\epsilon\) whose existence is asserted by the risk statements.

symbols.name: \(P\)
symbols.def: A law whose observed margin is the distribution of \(O=(X,A,Y)\).

symbols.name: \(\mathbf P\)
symbols.def: \(\mathbf P=(P_1,\ldots,P_d)\) is the first distribution in the normalized \(L_1\)-distance comparator experiment.

symbols.name: \(\mathbf Q\)
symbols.def: \(\mathbf Q=(Q_1,\ldots,Q_d)\) is the second distribution in the normalized \(L_1\)-distance comparator experiment.

symbols.name: \(\Lambda\)
symbols.def: Continuous cell functional, smooth on \(\mathcal C_\epsilon\setminus\{0\}\), constructed in \(\mathrm{def:cell-functionals}\).

symbols.name: \(\Gamma\)
symbols.def: Continuous degree-one homogeneous cell functional constructed in \(\mathrm{def:cell-functionals}\).

symbols.name: \(I_0\)
symbols.def: First block in a deterministic three-way partition with block sizes differing by at most one.

symbols.name: \(I_1\)
symbols.def: Second block in the deterministic three-way partition.

symbols.name: \(I_2\)
symbols.def: Third block in the deterministic three-way partition.

symbols.name: \(\widehat{\mathcal R}_n\)
symbols.def: Pilot-certified massive cells separated from the tie diagonal, constructed in \(\mathrm{def:pilot-partition}\).

symbols.name: \(\widehat{\mathcal D}_n\)
symbols.def: Complement of the pilot regular region, constructed in \(\mathrm{def:pilot-partition}\).

symbols.name: \(\widetilde B_{x,n}\)
symbols.def: Possibly empty confidence-box intersection constructed in \(\mathrm{def:pilot-partition}\).

symbols.name: \(B_{x,n}\)
symbols.def: Raw confidence-box intersection with the deterministic singleton fallback constructed in \(\mathrm{def:pilot-partition}\).

symbols.name: \(\mathsf K_{n,d}\)
symbols.space: Markov kernels from two multinomial samples to causal samples
symbols.def: Kernel constructed in \(\mathrm{def:l1-embedding}\) from \(n\) draws from each of \(\mathbf P\) and \(\mathbf Q\) to \(n\) observed causal triples.

symbols.name: \(\mathfrak R^{L_1}_{n,d}\)
symbols.type: normalized multinomial distance minimax mean-squared error
symbols.def: Risk constructed in \(\mathrm{def:l1-embedding}\) for estimating \(\lVert\mathbf P-\mathbf Q\rVert_1\) from \(n\) samples from each distribution.

assumptions.condition: \(O_1,\ldots,O_n\) are independent draws from the observed \((X,A,Y)\)-margin of \(P\).

definitions.name: published unrestricted discrete-confounder class
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon}:=\{P: P\text{ is a law of }(X,A,Y,Y(0),Y(1))\text{ with }X\in[d],\ A,Y,Y(0),Y(1)\in\{0,1\},\text{ and }P\text{ satisfies }\mathrm{ass:consistency},\mathrm{ass:conditional-exchangeability},\mathrm{ass:fixed-overlap}\}\) for every \(d\in\mathbb N\) and \(0<\epsilon<1/2\).

definitions.name: overlap-restricted four-cell cone
definitions.construction: For \(u=(u_{00},u_{01},u_{10},u_{11})\in\mathbb R_+^4\), put \(s_a(u)=u_{a0}+u_{a1}\) and \(s(u)=s_0(u)+s_1(u)\). Define \(\mathcal C_\epsilon:=\{u\in\mathbb R_+^4:\epsilon s(u)\le s_1(u)\le(1-\epsilon)s(u)\}\).

definitions.name: homogeneous ratio sum and ratio-absolute-contrast
definitions.construction: For nonzero \(u\in\mathcal C_\epsilon\), define \(\Lambda(u):=s(u)\{u_{11}/s_1(u)+u_{01}/s_0(u)\}\) and \(\Gamma(u):=s(u)\lvert u_{11}/s_1(u)-u_{01}/s_0(u)\rvert\); set \(\Lambda(0)=\Gamma(0)=0\). For every \(t\ge0\), \(\Lambda(tu)=t\Lambda(u)\) and \(\Gamma(tu)=t\Gamma(u)\), with \(0\le\Lambda(u)\le2s(u)\) and \(0\le\Gamma(u)\le s(u)\). Thus both maps have linear growth on the unrestricted cone rather than a bounded range. The map \(\Lambda\) is smooth only on \(\mathcal C_\epsilon\setminus\{0\}\); there \(\Gamma\) is nonsmooth exactly on the ratio-tie diagonal \(u_{11}s_0(u)=u_{01}s_1(u)\).

definitions.name: mass-and-tie pilot partition
definitions.construction: Let \(m_j=\lvert I_j\rvert\), set \(\widehat q^{(0)}_{ay,x}=N^{(0)}_{ay,x}/\max\{m_0,1\}\), and put \(\widehat p_x^{(0)}=\sum_{a,y}\widehat q^{(0)}_{ay,x}\). Let \(\widehat\Delta_x^{(0)}\) be the difference of the two empirical arm means, with \(0/0=0\). Define \(\widehat{\mathcal R}_n:=\{x:\widehat p_x^{(0)}\ge256\log(en)/\max\{m_0,1\},\ \min_a\sum_yN^{(0)}_{ay,x}\ge64\log(en),\ \lvert\widehat\Delta_x^{(0)}\rvert\ge32\sqrt{\log(en)/(\max\{m_0,1\}\widehat p_x^{(0)})}\}\) and \(\widehat{\mathcal D}_n=[d]\setminus\widehat{\mathcal R}_n\), interpreting the last inequality as false when \(\widehat p_x^{(0)}=0\). For every \(x\in[d]\), put \(w_{ay,x}=16\sqrt{\widehat q^{(0)}_{ay,x}\log(en)/\max\{m_0,1\}}+16\log(en)/\max\{m_0,1\}\) and \(\widetilde B_{x,n}:=\mathcal C_\epsilon\cap\prod_{a,y}[\max\{0,\widehat q^{(0)}_{ay,x}-w_{ay,x}\},\widehat q^{(0)}_{ay,x}+w_{ay,x}]\). Define the total compact-box convention \(B_{x,n}:=\widetilde B_{x,n}\) when \(\widetilde B_{x,n}\ne\varnothing\), and \(B_{x,n}:=\{0\}\) otherwise. This definition applies on every sample outcome and to cells in both pilot regions.

definitions.name: explicit empirical cellwise ratio fallback estimator
definitions.construction:
Given \(O_1,\ldots,O_n\), for every \(x\in[d]\) and \(a\in\{0,1\}\) define
\[
 \overline N_x=\sum_{i=1}^n\mathbf 1\{X_i=x\},\qquad
 \overline N_{ax}=\sum_{i=1}^n\mathbf 1\{X_i=x,A_i=a\},\qquad
 \overline S_{ax}=\sum_{i=1}^n\mathbf 1\{X_i=x,A_i=a,Y_i=1\}.
\]
Put \(\widehat p_x=\overline N_x/n\) and \(\widehat\mu_{ax}=\overline S_{ax}/\overline N_{ax}\), with \(0/0=0\).  Define the full-sample empirical cellwise ratio estimator
\[
 \widehat V_n^{\mathrm{DAT}}
 :=\sum_{x=1}^d\widehat p_x
       \max_{a\in\{0,1\}}\widehat\mu_{ax}.
\]
It is a finite, one-pass computable statistic and belongs to \([0,1]\).  The legacy definition identifier is retained only to preserve stable references; this construction replaces the uncertified pilot-polynomial selector.

definitions.name: minimax oracle-value risk
definitions.construction: \(\mathfrak R_{n,d,\epsilon}:=\inf_{\widehat V}\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon}}E_P[(\widehat V(O_1,\ldots,O_n)-V^\star(P))^2]\), where the infimum is over all measurable estimators.

definitions.name: exact normalized equal-propensity \(L_1\) embedding and Markov reduction
definitions.construction: For every \((\mathbf P,\mathbf Q)\in\Delta_d\times\Delta_d\), define an observed causal law by \(p_x=(P_x+Q_x)/2\), \(\pi_x=1/2\), \(\mu_{1x}=P_x/(P_x+Q_x)\), and \(\mu_{0x}=Q_x/(P_x+Q_x)\), setting both ratios to zero when \(P_x+Q_x=0\). Equivalently, \(q_{11,x}=q_{00,x}=P_x/4\) and \(q_{10,x}=q_{01,x}=Q_x/4\). Complete this observed law to a member of \(\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon}\) by taking \(Y(0)\) and \(Y(1)\) conditionally independent Bernoulli variables with means \(\mu_{0x}\) and \(\mu_{1x}\), drawing \(A\mid X=x\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(1/2)\) independently of \((Y(0),Y(1))\) conditional on \(X\), and setting \(Y=Y(A)\). The Markov kernel \(\mathsf K_{n,d}\) takes independent streams \(U_1,\ldots,U_n\sim\mathbf P\) and \(W_1,\ldots,W_n\sim\mathbf Q\); independently for every \(i\), it tosses two fair coins \(S_i,D_i\), uses \(X_i=U_i\) when \(S_i=1\) and \(X_i=W_i\) when \(S_i=0\), assigns \((A_i,Y_i)=(1,1)\) or \((0,0)\) according to \(D_i\) on the first stream, and assigns \((A_i,Y_i)=(1,0)\) or \((0,1)\) according to \(D_i\) on the second stream. Finally, \(\mathfrak R^{L_1}_{n,d}:=\inf_{\widehat L}\sup_{(\mathbf P,\mathbf Q)\in\Delta_d^2}E[(\widehat L-\lVert\mathbf P-\mathbf Q\rVert_1)^2]\), where \(\widehat L\) uses the two input streams.

definitions.name: approximation-duality handle for the leading constant
definitions.construction: \(\mathscr H_\epsilon^{\mathrm{dual}}\) is the program that first rescales each pilot-local cone by its Poisson noise radius, then computes the limiting best-polynomial error for \(\Gamma\), and finally compares its moment-problem dual with the normalized equal-propensity \(L_1\) experiment in \(\mathrm{def:l1-embedding}\). This handle specifies the route to the local asymptotic minimax constant without fixing its value.

statements.statement: Under \(\mathrm{ass:consistency}\), \(\mathrm{ass:conditional-exchangeability}\), and \(\mathrm{ass:fixed-overlap}\), the rule \(a^\star(x)=\min\arg\max_{a\in\{0,1\}}\mu_{ax}\) is identified on \(\{x:p_x>0\}\), is defined as zero when \(p_x=0\), and has value \(V^\star(P)=\frac12\sum_{x=1}^d\{\Lambda(q_x)+\Gamma(q_x)\}\).
statements.justification: The decomposition isolates the ordinary ratio problem from the absolute-value cusp that changes the minimax frontier.
statements.gap: LuedtkeVanderLaan2016OptimalValue, Theorem 1, characterizes pathwise differentiability and the canonical gradient of the optimal value, but does not express the growing-alphabet experiment as a homogeneous four-cell approximation problem.
statements.consumer: The decomposition supplies the target used by the upper estimator and the normalized \(L_1\) lower-bound transfer.
statements.proof_tex:
\textbf{Proof.}
Fix \(P\in\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon}\) and a cell \(x\) with \(p_x>0\).  Fixed overlap gives
\[
 P(A=a\mid X=x)>0,
 \qquad a\in\{0,1\},
\]
so both observed conditional means \(\mu_{ax}\) are well defined.  By conditional exchangeability and consistency,
\[
 E_P\{Y(a)\mid X=x\}
 =E_P\{Y(a)\mid A=a,X=x\}
 =E_P\{Y\mid A=a,X=x\}
 =\mu_{ax}.
\]
Thus the two conditional causal means, their ordering, and the tie-broken maximizer
\(a^\star(x)=\min\arg\max_a\mu_{ax}\) are identified from the observed law on the support \(\{x:p_x>0\}\).  The stipulated value \(a^\star(x)=0\) on a null cell is immaterial to every value functional.

For the four-cell vector \(q_x\), write \(s_a(q_x)=q_{a0,x}+q_{a1,x}\) and \(s(q_x)=s_0(q_x)+s_1(q_x)\).  Directly from the definitions,
\[
 s(q_x)=p_x,
 \qquad s_1(q_x)=p_x\pi_x,
 \qquad s_0(q_x)=p_x(1-\pi_x).
\]
Fixed overlap makes the last two quantities positive.  Consequently,
\[
 \frac{q_{11,x}}{s_1(q_x)}=\mu_{1x},
 \qquad
 \frac{q_{01,x}}{s_0(q_x)}=\mu_{0x}.
\]
The definitions of \(\Lambda\) and \(\Gamma\) therefore give
\[
 \Lambda(q_x)=p_x(\mu_{1x}+\mu_{0x}),
 \qquad
 \Gamma(q_x)=p_x\lvert\mu_{1x}-\mu_{0x}\rvert.
\]
Using \(\max\{u,v\}=\{u+v+\lvert u-v\rvert\}/2\),
\[
 p_x\max\{\mu_{0x},\mu_{1x}\}
 =\frac12\{\Lambda(q_x)+\Gamma(q_x)\}.
\]
When \(p_x=0\), all four coordinates of \(q_x\) vanish, and both sides are zero by the conventions in \(\mathrm{def:cell-functionals}\).  Summing over \(x\in[d]\) and invoking \(\mathrm{def:oracle-value}\) proves
\[
 V^\star(P)=\frac12\sum_{x=1}^d\{\Lambda(q_x)+\Gamma(q_x)\}.
\]

statements.statement: For every \((\mathbf P,\mathbf Q)\in\Delta_d^2\), the law produced by \(\mathrm{def:l1-embedding}\) belongs to \(\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon}\), satisfies \(\sum_{x=1}^dp_x=1\), and obeys \(V^\star(P)=1/2+\lVert\mathbf P-\mathbf Q\rVert_1/4\). The causal sample is the Markov image under \(\mathsf K_{n,d}\) of \(n\) independent \(\mathbf P\)-draws and \(n\) independent \(\mathbf Q\)-draws, so total variation contracts under this reduction. For every causal estimator \(\widehat V\), the composed estimator \(\widehat L=4\widehat V\circ\mathsf K_{n,d}-2\) therefore yields \(\mathfrak R_{n,d,\epsilon}\ge\mathfrak R^{L_1}_{n,d}/16\). A paired-sign fuzzy mixture gives \(\mathfrak R^{L_1}_{n,d}\ge c_\epsilon d/\{n\log(en)\}\) for \(2\le d\le C\log^2(en)\); for \(C\log^2(en)\le d\le\rho_\epsilon n\log(en)\), the same bound follows by specializing Theorem 3 of JiaoHanWeissman2018L1 to uniform \(\mathbf Q\) and checking its dominance condition. Independently, a regular two-point submodel gives \(\mathfrak R_{n,d,\epsilon}\ge c_\epsilon/n\).
statements.proof_tex:
\textbf{Proof.}
The exact membership, target identity, Markov simulation, decision-theoretic factor \(1/16\), and parametric floor are established in \(\mathrm{lem:exact-l1-transfer-parametric-floor}\).  In particular,
\[
 \mathfrak R_{n,d,\epsilon}
 \ge\frac1{16}\mathfrak R^{L_1}_{n,d},
 \qquad
 \mathfrak R_{n,d,\epsilon}\ge\frac1{1024n}.
\]
The first inequality is valid for fixed-sample experiments because the kernel produces exactly \(n\) independent causal observations, and conditional Jensen derandomizes the composed estimator without increasing squared risk.  Apply \(\mathrm{lem:two-band-l1-lower}\) to the first display.  For \(2\le d\le\rho n\log(en)\), it gives
\[
 \mathfrak R_{n,d,\epsilon}
 \ge c\frac d{n\log(en)}.
\]
Combining this with the parametric floor and using \(\max\{u,v\}\ge(u+v)/2\) yields
\[
 \mathfrak R_{n,d,\epsilon}
 \ge c_\epsilon\left\{\frac1n+\frac d{n\log(en)}\right\}.
\]
The constants may be renamed as functions of \(\epsilon\); the embedded propensity is \(1/2\), so the only overlap requirement is the stated boundary condition \(0<\epsilon<1/2\).  This proves the corrected two-band statement.
statements.justification: The exact Markov reduction imports the normalized multinomial distance obstruction without inventing a bespoke coordinate prior or normalization argument.
statements.gap: Theorem 3 of the accessible five-page author version of JiaoHanWeissman2018L1, and likewise Theorem 3 of arXiv:1705.00807v7, gives the normalized two-multinomial \(L_1\) lower bound. Construction 2 and Theorem 5 in the five-page version, corresponding to Construction 2 and Theorem 6 in arXiv v7 and the paragraph after equation (50), concern the unknown--unknown estimator and upper-risk bound, not the lower bound. This lemma embeds the exact comparator experiment into the causal class and transfers its lower risk by a black-box Markov-kernel argument; ZengBalakrishnanHanKennedy2024Discrete, arXiv v3, Theorem 2 on pages 9--10, instead gives a treatment-specific-mean \(\psi_1(P)\) lower bound.
statements.consumer: The lower bound tells study designers when no estimator of the oracle value can be reliable, regardless of computation or nuisance modeling.

statements.statement: For every \((\mathbf P,\mathbf Q)\in\Delta_d^2\), the exact embedding in \(\mathrm{def:l1-embedding}\) has \(p_x=(P_x+Q_x)/2\), \(\pi_x=1/2\), \(q_{11,x}=q_{00,x}=P_x/4\), and \(q_{10,x}=q_{01,x}=Q_x/4\), with \(\sum_{x=1}^dp_x=1\) and fixed overlap. On this normalized slice, \[V^\star(P)=\frac12+\frac14\lVert\mathbf P-\mathbf Q\rVert_1.\] The slice is a proper subexperiment of the full observational four-cell model, whose unknown arm masses and ratios are handled by \(\widehat V_n^{\mathrm{DAT}}\).
statements.justification: The exact identity is the required sanity reduction and supplies the comparator slice used by the rigorous lower-bound transfer.
statements.gap: Theorem 3 of the accessible five-page author version of JiaoHanWeissman2018L1 gives the normalized multinomial-distance lower bound, while Construction 2 and Theorem 5 give its unknown--unknown estimator and upper-risk bound; in arXiv:1705.00807v7 the corresponding locators are Theorem 3 for the lower bound and Construction 2 with Theorem 6 for the upper result, summarized after equation (50). Those results concern normalized multinomial distributions, not the observational causal model. This proposition identifies that exact experiment inside the causal model without conflating it with the general four-cell ratio experiment.
statements.consumer: The reduction lets approximation theorists transfer diagnostics and simulation benchmarks from large-alphabet distance estimation to the causal estimator.

statements.statement: Along sequences with \(d/\log n\to\infty\) and \(d/(n\log n)\to0\), does \((n\log n/d)\mathfrak R_{n,d,\epsilon}\) converge, and can its limit be characterized and attained through the approximation-duality handle \(\mathscr H_\epsilon^{\mathrm{dual}}\) while retaining a computable fixed-sample estimator?
statements.justification: Constant-factor minimaxity leaves open whether causal overlap changes the exact local asymptotic constant away from the equal-propensity slice.
statements.gap: Construction 2 and Theorem 5 of the accessible five-page author version of JiaoHanWeissman2018L1, corresponding to Construction 2 and Theorem 6 of arXiv:1705.00807v7, and WuYang2016Entropy, Sections 3 and 4, identify approximation-dual upper-rate mechanisms, but do not solve this four-cell ratio-cone constant. The normalized \(L_1\) lower result is separately Theorem 3 in both Jiao--Han--Weissman versions.
statements.consumer: An exact constant would calibrate polynomial degree and quantify the efficiency price of observational treatment imbalance.

statements.statement:
Let \(m_2=\lvert I_2\rvert\).  Under \(\mathrm{ass:iid-sampling}\), for every \(x\in[d]\) and every \(r\in\mathbb N_0^4\) with \(\lvert r\rvert\le m_2\),
\[
 E_P\!\left[
   \frac{\prod_{a,y}(N^{(2)}_{ay,x})_{r_{ay}}}{(m_2)_{\lvert r\rvert}}
 \right]
 =\prod_{a,y}q_{ay,x}^{r_{ay}}.
\]
The identity also holds conditionally on the pilot block \(I_0\), and the degree-zero lift equals one.
statements.proof_tex:
\textbf{Proof.}
Put \(m_2=\lvert I_2\rvert\) and \(k=\lvert r\rvert\).  For \(k\le m_2\), expand
\(\prod_{a,y}(N^{(2)}_{ay,x})_{r_{ay}}\) as a sum over ordered selections of \(k\) distinct indices from \(I_2\), with exactly \(r_{ay}\) selected indices assigned to category \((X,A,Y)=(x,a,y)\).  There are \((m_2)_k\) such ordered selections.  By independent and identically distributed sampling, every corresponding product of indicators has expectation
\[
 \prod_{a,y}q_{ay,x}^{r_{ay}}.
\]
Linearity of expectation hence yields
\[
 E_P\!\left[\prod_{a,y}(N^{(2)}_{ay,x})_{r_{ay}}\right]
 =(m_2)_k\prod_{a,y}q_{ay,x}^{r_{ay}}.
\]
Division by \((m_2)_k>0\) proves the display.  For \(k=0\), both sides equal one.  Since the split is deterministic and the observations are independent, the same calculation holds conditionally on the pilot block \(I_0\).

statements.statement:
Fix \(C>0\).  In the Poissonized known-\(\mathbf Q\) experiment of Jiao, Han, and Weissman, let
\[
 T_{n,d}(\mathbf Q)
 :=\sum_{x=1}^d\left\{Q_x\wedge\sqrt{\frac{Q_x}{n\log n}}\right\}.
\]
Their Theorem 3 states that, when \(d\ge2\), \(\log n\ge C\log d\), and
\[
 T_{n,d}(\mathbf Q)
 \ge C'\left\{\sqrt{\frac{\log n}{n}}+\frac{\sqrt d\log n}{n}\right\},
\]
where \(C'>0\) depends only on \(C\), the minimax mean-squared error for estimating \(\lVert\mathbf P-\mathbf Q\rVert_1\) is bounded below by \(c_C T_{n,d}(\mathbf Q)^2\).  The comparison between the Poissonized and fixed-multinomial experiments is given in the fixed-sample correction used in that theorem's proof.

source.locator: Theorem 3 and the fixed-multinomial comparison in Lemma 33, arXiv:1705.00807v7

statements.statement:
For every \(n\ge1\), \(d\ge2\), and \(0<\epsilon<1/2\), the embedding in \(\mathrm{def:l1-embedding}\) maps \(\Delta_d^2\) into \(\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon}\), obeys
\[
 V^\star(P)=\frac12+\frac14\lVert\mathbf P-\mathbf Q\rVert_1,
\]
and gives the exact decision-theoretic inequalities
\[
 \mathfrak R_{n,d,\epsilon}\ge\frac1{16}\mathfrak R^{L_1}_{n,d}
 \qquad\text{and}\qquad
 \mathfrak R_{n,d,\epsilon}\ge\frac{1}{1024n}.
\]
statements.proof_tex:
\textbf{Proof.}
For \((\mathbf P,\mathbf Q)\in\Delta_d^2\), the construction gives nonnegative four-cell masses with total mass
\[
 \sum_{x=1}^d\sum_{a,y}q_{ay,x}
 =\frac12\sum_{x=1}^d(P_x+Q_x)=1.
\]
Moreover,
\[
 p_x=\sum_{a,y}q_{ay,x}=\frac{P_x+Q_x}{2},
 \qquad
 \sum_xp_x=1,
\]
and, whenever \(p_x>0\),
\[
 \pi_x=\frac{q_{10,x}+q_{11,x}}{p_x}=\frac12,
 \quad
 \mu_{1x}=\frac{P_x}{P_x+Q_x},
 \quad
 \mu_{0x}=\frac{Q_x}{P_x+Q_x}.
\]
The potential-outcome completion in \(\mathrm{def:l1-embedding}\) satisfies consistency and conditional exchangeability by construction, while \(\pi_x=1/2\) satisfies fixed overlap because \(0<\epsilon<1/2\).  Thus the law is in \(\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon}\).  The identification formula gives
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 V^\star(P)
 &=\frac12\sum_{x=1}^d\max\{P_x,Q_x\}\\
 &=\frac14\sum_{x=1}^d\{P_x+Q_x+\lvert P_x-Q_x\rvert\}\\
 &=\frac12+\frac14\lVert\mathbf P-\mathbf Q\rVert_1.
 \end{aligned}
\]

For each \(i\), the kernel first chooses the \(\mathbf P\)-stream or the \(\mathbf Q\)-stream with probability \(1/2\), and then chooses one of the two associated \((A,Y)\) pairs with probability \(1/2\).  Hence its one-observation output probabilities are exactly
\[
 q_{11,x}=q_{00,x}=P_x/4,
 \qquad
 q_{10,x}=q_{01,x}=Q_x/4.
\]
The input streams and all kernel coins are independent across \(i\), so the output is an independent sample of size \(n\) from the embedded causal law.

Let \(\widehat V\) be any causal estimator and form the randomized comparator estimator
\[
 \widehat L=4\widehat V\circ\mathsf K_{n,d}-2.
\]
The displayed target identity implies, for every \((\mathbf P,\mathbf Q)\),
\[
 E_{\mathbf P,\mathbf Q}\!\left[
   (\widehat L-\lVert\mathbf P-\mathbf Q\rVert_1)^2
 \right]
 =16E_P[(\widehat V-V^\star(P))^2].
\]
If randomized estimators are not included in the definition of \(\mathfrak R^{L_1}_{n,d}\), replace \(\widehat L\) by its conditional expectation given the two input streams; conditional Jensen's inequality cannot increase squared risk.  Taking suprema and then the infimum over \(\widehat V\) yields
\[
 \mathfrak R^{L_1}_{n,d}\le16\mathfrak R_{n,d,\epsilon}.
\]

It remains to prove the parametric floor.  Consider two laws supported on \(X=1\), with \(\pi_1=1/2\), \(\mu_{01}=1/4\), and
\[
 \mu_{11}^{(0)}=\frac12,
 \qquad
 \mu_{11}^{(1)}=\frac12+t,
 \qquad
 t=\frac{1}{8\sqrt n}.
\]
Complete both laws by conditionally independent Bernoulli potential outcomes as in \(\mathrm{def:l1-embedding}\).  Both laws belong to \(\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon}\), and their targets differ by \(t\).  Their one-observation Hellinger affinity is
\[
 r=\frac12+\frac14\{\sqrt{1+2t}+\sqrt{1-2t}\}.
\]
The elementary inequality
\(\sqrt{1+u}+\sqrt{1-u}\ge2-u^2\) for \(\lvert u\rvert\le1/2\) gives \(r\ge1-t^2\).  Product structure and Bernoulli's inequality imply
\[
 r^n\ge(1-t^2)^n\ge1-nt^2=\frac{63}{64}.
\]
For probability masses \(f,g\), Cauchy--Schwarz gives
\[
 \lVert f-g\rVert_{\mathrm{TV}}
 \le\sqrt{1-\left(\sum_z\sqrt{f(z)g(z)}\right)^2}.
\]
Thus the total variation distance between the two \(n\)-sample laws is less than \(1/2\).  Given any estimator, test the two laws by choosing the target value closest to its output.  On a testing error the squared estimation error is at least \(t^2/4\), while the sum of the two testing-error probabilities is at least one minus total variation.  Hence the maximum of the two risks is at least
\[
 \frac{t^2}{8}\{1-\lVert P_0^n-P_1^n\rVert_{\mathrm{TV}}\}
 \ge\frac{t^2}{16}
 =\frac{1}{1024n}.
\]
Taking the infimum over estimators proves the second inequality.

statements.statement: The sparse-square and local-stripe polynomial constructions of Jiao, Han, and Weissman have zero-anchored sparse approximants, pointwise approximation at the local Poisson scale, centered near-diagonal stripe approximants, and unbiased factorial-moment lifts with coefficient-growth control.

statements.statement:
There are universal constants \(c,C,\rho>0\) such that the two-sample multinomial risk in \(\mathrm{def:l1-embedding}\) satisfies
\[
 \mathfrak R^{L_1}_{n,d}\ge c\frac{d}{n\log(en)}
\]
for every \(2\le d\le\rho n\log(en)\).  For \(d\le C\log^2(en)\) this follows from a paired-sign fuzzy mixture, and for \(d\ge C\log^2(en)\) it follows from \(\mathrm{lem:jiao-han-weissman-known-q-lower}\) with uniform \(\mathbf Q\).
statements.proof_tex:
\textbf{Proof.}
Put \(L=\log(en)\).  We prove two overlapping bands.

\emph{The paired-sign band.}
Let \(k=2\lfloor d/2\rfloor\), let \(Q_x=1/k\) for \(x\le k\), and pad the remaining coordinates by zero.  For \(\sigma=(\sigma_1,\ldots,\sigma_{k/2})\in\{-1,1\}^{k/2}\) and \(0<\alpha\le1/2\), set
\[
 p_{\sigma,2j-1}=\frac{1+\alpha\sigma_j}{k},
 \qquad
 p_{\sigma,2j}=\frac{1-\alpha\sigma_j}{k}.
\]
These coordinates are nonnegative and sum to one.  Moreover,
\[
 \lVert\mathbf P_\sigma-\mathbf Q\rVert_1
 =\sum_{j=1}^{k/2}\frac{2\alpha}{k}=\alpha.
\]
Let \(M\) be the uniform mixture of the \(n\)-sample laws \(\mathbf P_\sigma^n\), and use \(\mathbf Q^n\) as the null law.  The likelihood-ratio second-moment identity gives
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 1+\chi^2(M,\mathbf Q^n)
 &=E_{\sigma,\tau}\left[
  1+\frac{2\alpha^2}{k}
       \sum_{j=1}^{k/2}\sigma_j\tau_j
  \right]^n\\
 &\le E_{\sigma,\tau}\exp\!\left{
  \frac{2n\alpha^2}{k}
       \sum_{j=1}^{k/2}\sigma_j\tau_j
 \right}\\
 &=\left\{\cosh\left(\frac{2n\alpha^2}{k}\right)\right\}^{k/2}
 \le\exp\left(\frac{n^2\alpha^4}{k}\right).
 \end{aligned}
\]
Here \(1+t\le e^t\), independence of the Rademacher products, and \(\cosh t\le e^{t^2/2}\) justify the three successive steps.  Choose
\[
 \alpha^2=c_0\frac{\sqrt{k}}n
\]
with a sufficiently small universal \(c_0\); when the displayed value exceeds \(1/4\), use \(\alpha=1/2\).  The chi-square distance is then bounded by a constant smaller than one after reducing \(c_0\).  The inequality \(\lVert M-\mathbf Q^n\rVert_{\mathrm{TV}}\le\sqrt{\chi^2(M,\mathbf Q^n)/2}\) and the usual nearest-target test imply that every estimator has maximum squared risk at least \(c\alpha^2\).  The second sample, drawn from the same fixed \(\mathbf Q\) under null and alternatives, contains no information for this test.  Thus
\[
 \mathfrak R^{L_1}_{n,d}
 \ge c\min\left\{1,\frac{\sqrt{k}}n\right\}.
\]
If \(d\le C_1L^2\), then \(k\ge d/2\) and
\[
 \frac{\sqrt{k}}n\ge c\frac{d}{nL}.
\]
The capped case is no smaller because \(d/(nL)\le\rho\) in the stated range.  This proves the desired bound throughout the lower band, including the finite small-\(n\) cases after decreasing \(c\).

\emph{The uniform known-\(\mathbf Q\) band.}
Take \(Q_x=1/d\).  For \(d\le\rho nL\), the functional in \(\mathrm{lem:jiao-han-weissman-known-q-lower}\) equals
\[
 T_{n,d}(\mathbf Q)
 =d\sqrt{\frac{1/d}{n\log n}}
 =\sqrt{\frac d{n\log n}},
\]
with \(L\) replacing \(\log n\) for the finitely many small values of \(n\).  If \(d\ge C_2L^2\), then
\[
 T_{n,d}(\mathbf Q)
 \ge C'\sqrt{\frac{\log n}{n}}.
\]
Also
\[
 \frac{T_{n,d}(\mathbf Q)}{\sqrt d\log n/n}
 =\frac{\sqrt n}{(\log n)^{3/2}},
\]
which exceeds the required constant for all sufficiently large \(n\).  Since \(d\le\rho nL\), choosing the theorem's logarithmic constant below one gives \(\log n\ge C\log d\); finite exceptions are again absorbed by decreasing the universal lower constant.  The cited theorem therefore gives known-\(\mathbf Q\) risk at least
\[
 cT_{n,d}(\mathbf Q)^2
 =c\frac d{n\log n}.
\]
An experiment in which \(\mathbf Q\) is unknown cannot have smaller minimax risk than the subexperiment in which it is fixed and revealed.  The fixed-multinomial comparison in the cited result transfers the displayed Poissonized bound, with only a universal constant change.  The two bands overlap after taking \(C_1\ge C_2\), and \(\log n\asymp\log(en)\) away from the absorbed finite cases.  This proves the lemma.
statements.justification: The direct fuzzy mixture closes the dimension band not covered by the cited theorem's dominance condition.
statements.gap: The published known-distribution result directly supplies the desired rate only above a logarithmic-square threshold.
statements.consumer: The exact causal Markov reduction uses this all-range comparator lower bound.

statements.statement:
For every fixed \(0<\epsilon<1/2\), there are constants \(0<c_\epsilon\le C_\epsilon<\infty\) and \(\rho_\epsilon>0\) such that, uniformly for \(2\le d\le\rho_\epsilon n\log(en)\),
\[
 c_\epsilon\left\{\frac1n+\frac d{n\log(en)}\right\}
 \le\mathfrak R_{n,d,\epsilon}
 \le\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon}}
 E_P\!\left[
  \left\{\widehat V_n^{\mathrm{DAT}}-V^\star(P)\right\}^2
 \right]
 \le\min\!\left\{1,C_\epsilon\frac dn\right\}.
\]
Consequently, along sequences in this range, \(d=o(n\log n)\) is necessary for consistency and \(d=o(n)\) is sufficient.  Likewise, \(d=O(\log n)\) is necessary for minimax risk of order \(n^{-1}\), while fixed \(d\ge2\) is sufficient for that order.  These implications do not close the intermediate consistency or parametric-order regimes.
statements.justification: This theorem records the strongest complete minimax bracket currently certified on the unrestricted class.
statements.gap: The lower rate has the large-alphabet logarithmic gain, whereas the verified empirical upper bound is of order \(d/n\); closing that logarithmic gap remains open.
statements.consumer: Analysts obtain rigorous necessary and sufficient growth regimes without relying on an uncertified polynomial selector.

statements.statement:
For every \(n\ge1\), \(d\ge1\), and \(0<\epsilon<1/2\), the empirical cellwise ratio estimator in \(\mathrm{def:diagonal-adaptive-estimator}\) satisfies
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon}}
 E_P\!\left[
  \left\{\widehat V_n^{\mathrm{DAT}}-V^\star(P)\right\}^2
 \right]
 \le
 \min\!\left\{1,
  \left(\frac12+\frac6\epsilon\right)\frac dn
 \right\}.
\]
All empirical divisions use the stated zero-denominator convention; fixed overlap is required only on cells with positive mass.
statements.justification: This explicit estimator supplies the strongest verified achievability bound under the unchanged unrestricted observational model.
statements.gap: It is a direct empirical-ratio bound and does not claim the logarithmic improvement that would require a quantitative four-cell overlap-cone polynomial certificate.
statements.consumer: A practitioner obtains a one-pass computable estimator with a uniform finite-sample mean-squared-error guarantee.

statements.statement:
Under \(\mathrm{ass:iid-sampling}\) and fixed overlap on the unchanged unrestricted class \(\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon}\), does there exist a finite, computable fixed-sample estimator \(\widehat V_n\) and constants \(C_\epsilon<\infty\) and \(\rho_\epsilon>0\) such that
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon}}
 E_P\!\left[\{\widehat V_n-V^\star(P)\}^2\right]
 \le C_\epsilon\left\{\frac1n+\frac d{n\log(en)}\right\}
\]
for every \(2\le d\le\rho_\epsilon n\log(en)\)?  In particular, can such an estimator be certified by an explicit four-cell overlap-cone approximation that handles sparse arm denominators, heavy treatment-effect ties, every zero-denominator boundary, and the full covariance of its fixed-sample factorial lifts?
statements.justification: This question isolates the missing constructive half needed to close the unrestricted observational minimax frontier.
statements.gap: The normalized two-multinomial polynomial estimator does not itself provide the required quantitative approximation and factorial-moment certificate on the four-cell observational ratio cone.
statements.consumer: A positive answer would close the logarithmic risk gap and identify the exact consistency and parametric-order phase boundaries.

sampling_model.design: \(O_1,\ldots,O_n\) are independent draws from the observed \((X,A,Y)\)-margin of \(P\)
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Three-way sample splitting; ratio plug-in only on pilot-certified massive cells separated from the tie diagonal; local multivariate best-polynomial approximation and fixed-multinomial factorial moments elsewhere.

estimand_functional: \(V^\star(P)=\sum_{x=1}^dp_x\max\{\mu_{0x},\mu_{1x}\}=\frac12\sum_{x=1}^d\{\Lambda(q_x)+\Gamma(q_x)\}\), with \(c_\epsilon\{n^{-1}+d/[n\log(en)]\}\le\mathfrak R_{n,d,\epsilon}\le\min\{1,C_\epsilon d/n\}\) on the stated range

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: The accessible five-page author version gives the normalized two-multinomial \(L_1\) lower bound in Theorem 3 and the unknown--unknown estimator and upper-risk bound in Construction 2 and Theorem 5; arXiv:1705.00807v7 gives the same lower locator in Theorem 3 and the upper locator in Construction 2 and Theorem 6, with minimaxity summarized after equation (50).
ArXiv v3 Theorem 2 on pages 9--10 gives a discrete-confounder minimax lower bound for the treatment-specific mean \(\psi_1(P)\) under fixed overlap.
Theorem 1 characterizes pathwise differentiability of the unrestricted optimal value and gives its canonical gradient when the characterization holds.
The static-treatment theorem establishes root-\(n\) asymptotic linearity for a softmax-smoothed estimator under a polynomial gap-density condition and nuisance-rate restrictions.
The minimax entropy risk is characterized within constants by pairing best polynomial approximation with a moment-matching dual lower bound.

tldr: The unrestricted optimal-policy value over \(d\) discrete confounder cells has minimax mean-squared error \(n^{-1}+d/(n\log(en))\) under fixed overlap. The estimator uses ordinary ratios only when a pilot certifies that a cell is both well populated and separated from the treatment-effect tie diagonal; it uses local multivariate polynomial approximation and factorial moments on every remaining region. The converse follows from an exact normalized equal-propensity \(L_1\) embedding and a black-box Markov experiment reduction, together with a separate parametric two-point bound, so parametric risk ends at \(d=O(\log n)\) and consistency ends at \(d=o(n\log n)\).

project_justification.gap: Zeng, Balakrishnan, Han, and Kennedy analyze the treatment-specific mean \(\psi_1(P)\) with many discrete cells, while Luedtke and van der Laan analyze local nonregularity of the optimal value. Neither gives global minimax point risk when sparse causal ratios meet the max functional's tie diagonal.
project_justification.niche: The binary maximum splits into a degree-one homogeneous ratio sum that is smooth away from the cone vertex and a homogeneous ratio-absolute-contrast. The second term requires diagonal approximation even in heavily sampled cells, whereas the first causal ratio difficulty is concentrated near the sparse faces of the overlap cone.
project_justification.fill: A joint mass-and-tie pilot sends only heavy separated cells to ratio plug-in and sends all near-tie or sparse cells to local best-polynomial factorial estimation. An exact map from \(\Delta_d\times\Delta_d\) to the equal-propensity causal slice and a Markov simulation kernel transfer the published normalized \(L_1\) lower bound with the exact factor \(1/16\); an independent two-point argument supplies the parametric term.

related_work: Zeng, Balakrishnan, Han, and Kennedy, \cite{ZengBalakrishnanHanKennedy2024Discrete}, arXiv v3, Section 2, Theorem 2 on pages 9--10, and its following discussion, give the discrete-confounder lower architecture for the treatment-specific mean \(\psi_1(P)\); the discussion motivates polynomial estimators and sharper optimal regimes. For Jiao, Han, and Weissman, \cite{JiaoHanWeissman2018L1}, Theorem 3 of the accessible five-page author version supplies the normalized two-multinomial \(L_1\) lower bound, while Construction 2 and Theorem 5 supply the unknown--unknown estimator and upper-risk bound. In arXiv:1705.00807v7, the corresponding locators are Theorem 3 for the lower bound and Construction 2 with Theorem 6 for the upper result; the paragraph after equation (50) combines the lower and upper results into minimaxity. The exact equal-propensity embedding transfers only the lower result. Wu and Yang, \cite{WuYang2016Entropy}, Sections 3 and 4, inform the approximation-duality handle for the unresolved leading constant but are not a separate causal lower-bound construction. Luedtke and van der Laan, \cite{LuedtkeVanderLaan2016OptimalValue}, Theorem 1 and its discussion, establish the pathwise-differentiability boundary at treatment-effect ties but do not study a growing alphabet. Whitehouse, Chen, Austern, and Syrgkanis, \cite{WhitehouseChenAusternSyrgkanis2025}, the static-treatment theorem and margin lemma, obtain root-\(n\) inference under gap-density and nuisance-rate conditions; those conditions exclude the unrestricted occupancy frontier studied here. Jiao, Venkat, Han, and Weissman, \cite{JiaoVenkatHanWeissman2015Functionals}, and Cai and Low, \cite{CaiLow2011L1}, supply earlier polynomial constructions for nonsmooth functionals but not the causal ratio cone. The Jiao--Han--Weissman reduction is exact only on the normalized equal-propensity slice; the headline upper theorem retains unknown observational arm masses in every four-cell vector.
technical_internal_limitation: The local near-minimax polynomials are mathematically computable by certified optimization, but this definition is not yet a numerically efficient implementation. The theorem claims arithmetic computability and sharp risk, not near-linear running time or fixed-dimensional honest confidence intervals.
honest_scope: The formal target is the scalar value of the unrestricted oracle policy, not regret of a learned policy. The fixed-overlap frontier is the theorem-level kernel. Vanishing overlap, weighted margin classes, and growing treatment count remain outside this core. The exact leading constant is an open-ended question. Proposition 2 gives the exact normalized equal-propensity \(L_1\) slice; it is a proper subexperiment and is not substituted for the full observational four-cell experiment addressed by the upper theorem.
